title: The record the game keeps for each monster
summary: Monsters in R.E.P.O. are described before they are placed: each one has a record with a name, a difficulty, a type, its health, its music cues and the presets for its own body.
body: A monster in R.E.P.O. is described before it is put in a level. There is a checklist record for each one, and it carries the monster's name, a difficulty and a type, so the game knows what it is dealing with as data rather than in code.

The record fixes where the monster is centred and what it looks at when it kills. Keeping both on the record is how the game can line up a finishing blow without every monster needing its own script for it.
It carries the monster's music cues. There is a stinger for being sighted and a separate piece of music for when the monster is near, which is why the soundtrack can react before anything is visible.

It carries the monster's health. There is a maximum, a mesh the health is shown on, and a set of health objects for being hurt, for dying and for an impact, so what happens when a monster is damaged is configured rather than assumed.

It says whether the monster has a body of its own. A flag decides that, and the record goes on to give it a physics preset and an audio preset, which is how two monsters can sound and fall differently while sharing one system.

It lists the colliders that body uses and how it follows things: a follow behaviour, a custom gravity, a way of being grabbed, and position and rotation following. That is the whole vocabulary for making a monster move physically.
Because the record includes the difficulty and the type, the same body and the same music can be reused with a different setting, which is why the monsters can be tuned without being rebuilt.

None of this is the monster itself. The record is the description and the creature in the level is an instance of it, which is why a monster can be taken out and put back without forgetting what it is.
What this entry does not tell you: how much health any monster has, what its difficulty is set to, or what its music sounds like. We have not verified those, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Each monster has a record with a name, a difficulty and a type.
The record holds where the monster is centred and what it looks at when it kills.
It holds a stinger for a sighting and the music for when the monster is near.
It holds health: a maximum, the mesh the health is shown on, and objects for being hurt, dying and an impact.
facts.evidence: identifiers: healthMax, healthMeshParent, healthOnHurt, healthOnDeath, healthImpact, healthObject

facts.claim: It says whether the monster has a rigid body and gives it physics and audio presets.
It lists the body's colliders and its follow behaviours, including custom gravity, grabbing, position following and rotation following.
facts.evidence: identifiers: rigidbodyColliders, rigidbodyFollow, rigidbodyCustomGravity, rigidbodyGrab, rigidbodyPositionFollow, rigidbodyRotationFollow
